title: Running revenue by month
task: Set result to a Series indexed by 'YYYY-MM' with cumulative delivered revenue (2 dp), sorted by month.
answer:
d = orders[orders['status'] == 'delivered']
m = d.groupby(d['order_date'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m'))['total_amount'].sum().sort_index()
result = m.cumsum().round(2)

title: Month-over-month change
task: Set result to a Series of month-over-month change in delivered revenue (2 dp), first month NaN dropped, sorted by month.
answer:
d = orders[orders['status'] == 'delivered']
m = d.groupby(d['order_date'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m'))['total_amount'].sum().sort_index()
result = m.diff().dropna().round(2)

title: 3-month moving average of order counts
task: Set result to a Series of 3-month rolling mean of monthly order counts (2 dp), sorted by month, NaNs dropped.
answer:
m = orders['order_date'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m').value_counts().sort_index()
result = m.rolling(3).mean().dropna().round(2)

title: Days between consecutive orders per customer
task: Set result to a DataFrame with customer_id, order_id, gap_days for every order that has a previous order by the same customer (sorted by order_date, order_id).
answer:
o = orders.sort_values(['customer_id', 'order_date', 'order_id']).copy()
o['prev'] = o.groupby('customer_id')['order_date'].shift()
o['gap_days'] = (o['order_date'] - o['prev']).dt.days
result = o.dropna(subset=['gap_days'])[['customer_id', 'order_id', 'gap_days']].astype({'gap_days': int}).reset_index(drop=True)

title: Most recent order per customer
task: Set result to a DataFrame of each customer's latest order (columns customer_id, order_id, order_date), ties by higher order_id.
answer: result = orders.sort_values(['order_date', 'order_id'], ascending=[False, False]).drop_duplicates('customer_id')[['customer_id', 'order_id', 'order_date']].sort_values('customer_id').reset_index(drop=True)

title: Customer spend quartiles
task: Set result to a DataFrame with customer_id, total_spend (2 dp) and quartile (1 = highest spend) using pd.qcut into 4 bins, sorted by customer_id.
answer:
s = orders.groupby('customer_id')['total_amount'].sum().round(2).rename('total_spend').reset_index()
s['quartile'] = pd.qcut(s['total_spend'], 4, labels=[4, 3, 2, 1]).astype(int)
result = s.sort_values('customer_id').reset_index(drop=True)

title: Product share within category
task: Set result to a DataFrame with category, name and pct_of_category (1 dp) = product revenue / category revenue * 100, over all order items.
answer:
m = order_items.merge(products[['product_id', 'name', 'category']], on='product_id')
m['rev'] = m['quantity'] * m['unit_price']
g = m.groupby(['category', 'name'], as_index=False)['rev'].sum()
g['pct_of_category'] = (g['rev'] / g.groupby('category')['rev'].transform('sum') * 100).round(1)
result = g[['category', 'name', 'pct_of_category']]

title: Repeat-purchase rate by signup year
task: Set result to a Series indexed by signup year with the % of customers (with ≥1 order) who have 2+ orders, 1 dp.
hint: Order counts per customer joined to customers.
answer:
oc = orders.groupby('customer_id').size().rename('n')
m = customers.merge(oc, left_on='customer_id', right_index=True)
m['year'] = m['signup_date'].dt.year
result = (m.groupby('year')['n'].apply(lambda s: (s >= 2).mean() * 100)).round(1)

title: Customers active in consecutive months
task: Set result to a Series indexed by 'YYYY-MM' with the number of customers who ordered in that month and the previous calendar month, only months with count > 0, sorted.
hint: Set of (customer, month) pairs; check previous month membership.
answer:
um = orders.assign(month=orders['order_date'].dt.to_period('M'))[['customer_id', 'month']].drop_duplicates()
pairs = set(zip(um['customer_id'], um['month']))
um['retained'] = [(c, m - 1) in pairs for c, m in zip(um['customer_id'], um['month'])]
r = um.groupby('month')['retained'].sum()
r = r[r > 0]
r.index = r.index.astype(str)
result = r.astype(int)

title: RFM table
task: Set result to a DataFrame indexed by customer_id with recency_days (days from last order to 2025-07-31), frequency (order count) and monetary (2 dp), sorted by customer_id.
hint: agg with named aggregations then compute recency.
answer:
g = orders.groupby('customer_id').agg(last=('order_date', 'max'), frequency=('order_id', 'count'), monetary=('total_amount', 'sum'))
g['recency_days'] = (pd.Timestamp('2025-07-31') - g['last']).dt.days
g['monetary'] = g['monetary'].round(2)
result = g[['recency_days', 'frequency', 'monetary']].sort_index()

title: Products making up 80% of revenue
task: Set result to a Series of product names (in descending revenue order) whose cumulative revenue share reaches 80% — include the product that crosses 80%.
hint: sort desc, cumsum/total, keep where previous cumulative < 0.8.
answer:
m = order_items.merge(products[['product_id', 'name']], on='product_id')
rev = (m['quantity'] * m['unit_price']).groupby(m['name']).sum().sort_values(ascending=False)
prev = rev.cumsum().shift(fill_value=0) / rev.sum()
result = pd.Series(rev[prev < 0.8].index)

title: Products bought together
task: Set result to a DataFrame with columns product_a, product_b (ids, a < b) and times_together (distinct orders containing both), keeping pairs with 2+ orders, sorted by times_together desc then product_a, product_b.
answer:
a = order_items[['order_id', 'product_id']].drop_duplicates()
p = a.merge(a, on='order_id')
p = p[p['product_id_x'] < p['product_id_y']]
g = p.groupby(['product_id_x', 'product_id_y'])['order_id'].nunique().reset_index()
g.columns = ['product_a', 'product_b', 'times_together']
result = g[g['times_together'] >= 2].sort_values(['times_together', 'product_a', 'product_b'], ascending=[False, True, True]).reset_index(drop=True)

title: Wide to long
task: Given wide = pd.DataFrame({'region': ['N','S'], 'q1': [10, 20], 'q2': [15, 25]}), set result to the long form with columns region, quarter, sales, sorted by region then quarter.
answer:
wide = pd.DataFrame({'region': ['N','S'], 'q1': [10, 20], 'q2': [15, 25]})
result = wide.melt(id_vars='region', var_name='quarter', value_name='sales').sort_values(['region', 'quarter']).reset_index(drop=True)

title: Status pivot with totals
task: Set result to pd.crosstab(country, status) with margins=True (margins_name 'Total').
answer:
m = orders.merge(customers[['customer_id', 'country']], on='customer_id')
result = pd.crosstab(m['country'], m['status'], margins=True, margins_name='Total')

title: Name initials
task: Set result to a Series of initials like 'SC' for each customer (first letter of first and last name, uppercase).
hint: str[0] on each column, concatenate, str.upper().
answer: result = (customers['first_name'].str[0] + customers['last_name'].str[0]).str.upper()

title: Normalise emails
context: Lowercase and strip; count how many changed.
task: Set result to the number of non-null emails that differ from their lowercased, stripped version.
answer:
e = customers['email'].dropna()
result = int((e != e.str.lower().str.strip()).sum())

title: Months with zero orders
task: Set result to a Series indexed by every month from 2024-01 to 2025-07 ('YYYY-MM') with order counts, including zeros.
answer:
m = orders['order_date'].dt.to_period('M').value_counts().sort_index()
idx = pd.period_range('2024-01', '2025-07', freq='M')
r = m.reindex(idx, fill_value=0)
r.index = r.index.astype(str)
result = r.astype(int)

title: Longest streak of consecutive order days
task: Set result to the length (int) of the longest run of consecutive calendar days that each had at least one order.
hint: Distinct dates sorted; group id = date - rank; max group size.
answer:
d = orders['order_date'].dt.normalize().drop_duplicates().sort_values().reset_index(drop=True)
grp = (d - pd.to_timedelta(range(len(d)), unit='D'))
result = int(grp.value_counts().max())

title: Fan-out check
task: Set result to a DataFrame indexed by category with revenue (2 dp, from order_items) and review_count, computed separately (no double counting).
hint: Two aggregations then join on category.
answer:
m = order_items.merge(products[['product_id', 'category']], on='product_id')
rev = (m['quantity'] * m['unit_price']).groupby(m['category']).sum().round(2).rename('revenue')
rc = reviews.merge(products[['product_id', 'category']], on='product_id').groupby('category').size().rename('review_count')
result = pd.concat([rev, rc], axis=1).fillna(0).astype({'review_count': int})

title: Per-customer summary with apply
task: Set result to a DataFrame indexed by customer_id with columns first_order, last_order (dates) and orders (count), sorted by customer_id.
answer: result = orders.groupby('customer_id').agg(first_order=('order_date', 'min'), last_order=('order_date', 'max'), orders=('order_id', 'count')).sort_index()

title: Vectorise a loop
context: Replace a Python loop with vector maths.
task: Set result to the delivered revenue per order_id as a Series (2 dp) computed without any Python for-loop, from order_items and orders.
answer:
m = order_items.merge(orders[['order_id', 'status']], on='order_id')
m = m[m['status'] == 'delivered']
result = (m['quantity'] * m['unit_price']).groupby(m['order_id']).sum().round(2)

title: Weighted average price
task: Set result to the quantity-weighted average unit_price across order_items, rounded to 2 decimals.
answer: result = round(float(np.average(order_items['unit_price'], weights=order_items['quantity'])), 2)

title: Percentiles
task: Set result to a list of the 25th, 50th and 90th percentiles of orders total_amount, each rounded to 2 decimals.
answer: result = [round(float(x), 2) for x in np.percentile(orders['total_amount'], [25, 50, 90])]

title: Outliers by z-score
task: Set result to the number of orders whose total_amount z-score (population std) exceeds 2 in absolute value.
answer:
x = orders['total_amount'].to_numpy()
z = (x - x.mean()) / x.std()
result = int((np.abs(z) > 2).sum())

title: A tiny Order class
task: Define class Order with __init__(self, items) where items is a list of (price, qty), and a method total() returning the sum of price*qty. Set result to Order([(10, 2), (5.5, 4)]).total().
hint: sum(p*q for p, q in self.items).

title: Running total generator
task: Define running_total(xs) that yields the cumulative sum, and set result to list(running_total([3, 1, 4, 1, 5])).
hint: Keep a total, yield after each add.

title: Flatten arbitrarily nested lists
task: Define flatten(x) that flattens nested lists of any depth; set result to flatten([1, [2, [3, [4]], 5], [6]]).

title: Parse with try/except
task: Given raw = ['12', '3.5', 'x', '', '7'], set result to the list of floats that parse successfully.

title: All pairs
task: Set result to the list of all 2-element combinations of ['a','b','c','d'] as tuples.
answer: result = list(itertools.combinations(['a', 'b', 'c', 'd'], 2))

title: Business days between dates
task: Set result to the number of weekdays (Mon–Fri) from 2025-03-10 to 2025-03-28 inclusive, using the datetime module.
answer:
start, end = datetime.date(2025, 3, 10), datetime.date(2025, 3, 28)
result = sum(1 for i in range((end - start).days + 1) if (start + datetime.timedelta(days=i)).weekday() < 5)

title: Two-sum
task: Given nums = [2, 7, 11, 15] and target = 26, set result to the tuple of indices (i, j) with i < j such that nums[i] + nums[j] == target.

title: Top-k frequent words
task: Given text = 'b a c a b a d c', set result to the 2 most common words as a list of (word, count), ties broken alphabetically.
answer:
text = 'b a c a b a d c'
c = Counter(text.split())
result = sorted(c.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0]))[:2]

title: Records for an API
task: Set result to the 3 cheapest products as a list of dicts with keys name and price (sorted by price ascending).
answer: result = products.nsmallest(3, 'price')[['name', 'price']].to_dict('records')
